column1: # Format: anchor TAB synonym TAB antonym
# Test:   for an encoder useful in our architecture, cos(anchor, synonym)
#         should be GREATER than cos(anchor, antonym).
# Score per row: cos(anchor, synonym) − cos(anchor, antonym).
# Mean score across rows = encoder's antonym-separation quality.
# Higher = encoder cleanly separates synonym vs antonym geometry.
# Why this matters here: our concept operators apply learned shifts in
# the encoder's latent space. If the encoder buries antonyms inside
# synonym clusters (e.g. cos(warm, sick) ≈ cos(warm, cool) — the
# documented failure mode in RESULTS.md "Multi-axial re-diagnosis"),
# no operator architecture can win retrieval. This suite gives a
# scalar score per encoder that flags this risk before it bites.
